general_concept_gap.title: General Concept Gap
general_concept_gap.explanation: Some of your answers suggest gaps in the core ideas for this topic. Revisit the key definitions, diagrams, and example questions before trying a new quiz.
general_concept_gap.focus_area: Review the main definitions and standard diagrams in your textbook for this topic.

angle_from_surface.title: Angles Measured from Surface
angle_from_surface.explanation: Angle of incidence and angle of reflection are never measured from the mirror surface itself. Both angles are always measured from the NORMAL drawn perpendicular to the mirror.
angle_from_surface.focus_area: Draw the normal as a perpendicular line to the mirror and shade the angles between the rays and this normal, not the mirror surface.

reflection_not_equal.title: i and r Must Be Equal
reflection_not_equal.explanation: According to the first law of reflection, the angle of incidence is exactly equal to the angle of reflection (i = r) when light reflects from a smooth surface.
reflection_not_equal.focus_area: Show incident and reflected rays making equal angles with the normal, and explicitly label i and r as equal.

normal_orientation_wrong.title: Normal Drawn Incorrectly
normal_orientation_wrong.explanation: The normal is an imaginary line drawn perpendicular to the mirror surface at the point where the ray hits, not parallel or at any random angle.
normal_orientation_wrong.focus_area: Highlight the mirror surface and then draw the normal at 90° to it exactly at the point of incidence.

plane_not_same.title: Rays Not in Same Plane
plane_not_same.explanation: The incident ray, reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence must all lie in the same plane. If you draw them in different planes, the second law of reflection is violated.
plane_not_same.focus_area: Show the mirror, normal and both rays drawn together on a single flat surface to emphasize they are coplanar.

concave_convex_confusion.title: Concave vs Convex Identification
concave_convex_confusion.explanation: The reflecting surface of a concave mirror is curved inwards (like the inside of a spoon), while for a convex mirror, it is curved outwards (like the back of a spoon).
concave_convex_confusion.focus_area: Differentiate between the reflecting side and the polished/shaded side for both types of mirrors.

pole_confusion.title: Pole Location
pole_confusion.explanation: The pole (P) is the geometric center of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror. It lies on the surface of the mirror, not inside or outside it.
pole_confusion.focus_area: Mark the exact midpoint of the mirror's aperture and label it as P.

center_of_curvature_confusion.title: Center of Curvature Position
center_of_curvature_confusion.explanation: The center of curvature (C) is the center of the hollow sphere of which the mirror is a part. It is not a part of the mirror surface itself.
center_of_curvature_confusion.focus_area: Draw the full imaginary sphere from which the mirror is cut and mark its center C.

radius_focal_relation_wrong.title: R and f Relation Error
radius_focal_relation_wrong.explanation: For spherical mirrors of small aperture, the radius of curvature is found to be equal to twice the focal length (R = 2f).
radius_focal_relation_wrong.focus_area: Show the distance CP (Radius R) and the distance FP (Focal length f) and explain that f = R/2.

principal_axis_confusion.title: Principal Axis
principal_axis_confusion.explanation: The principal axis is a straight line passing through the pole and the center of curvature of a spherical mirror. It is normal to the mirror at its pole.
principal_axis_confusion.focus_area: Draw a long straight line passing through both P and C to represent the principal axis.

focus_definition_wrong.title: Principal Focus
focus_definition_wrong.explanation: For a concave mirror, rays parallel to the principal axis actually meet at a point called the principal focus (F). For a convex mirror, they appear to diverge from it.
focus_definition_wrong.focus_area: Show parallel rays converging to F for concave, and appearing to come from F behind the mirror for convex.

image_position_wrong.title: Incorrect Image Position
image_position_wrong.explanation: The position of the image depends strictly on the position of the object relative to P, F, and C. Using the mirror formula or standard ray tracing reveals the exact location.
image_position_wrong.focus_area: Show the correct ray tracing intersection for the given object position to prove where the image must form.

image_size_wrong.title: Incorrect Image Size
image_size_wrong.explanation: The size of the image (magnified or diminished) depends on where the object is placed. For example, an object beyond C forms a diminished image, while an object between C and F forms an enlarged one.
image_size_wrong.focus_area: Compare the height of the object arrow to the height of the image arrow formed by the intersecting rays.

image_nature_wrong.title: Real vs Virtual Confusion
image_nature_wrong.explanation: A real image forms when reflected rays actually intersect in front of the mirror. A virtual image forms when rays diverge and only appear to intersect behind the mirror.
image_nature_wrong.focus_area: Highlight whether the actual solid rays meet (real) or if dashed, extended rays meet behind the mirror (virtual).

ray_tracing_rule_violation.title: Incorrect Ray Tracing
ray_tracing_rule_violation.explanation: There are strict rules for ray tracing: a ray parallel to the principal axis reflects through the focus; a ray through the focus reflects parallel; a ray through the center of curvature reflects back along its path.
ray_tracing_rule_violation.focus_area: Draw one standard ray correctly and emphasize the rule it follows upon hitting the mirror.

convex_real_image_myth.title: Convex Real Image Myth
convex_real_image_myth.explanation: Believing that a convex mirror can form a real image. Convex mirrors always diverge light and form virtual, erect, and diminished images behind the mirror.
convex_real_image_myth.focus_area: Verify that reflected rays from a convex mirror always diverge.

convex_size_confusion.title: Convex Image Size Error
convex_size_confusion.explanation: Thinking a convex mirror can form a magnified or same-sized image. Images formed by convex mirrors are always diminished.
convex_size_confusion.focus_area: Observe the image size formed by a convex mirror.

real_virtual_confusion.title: Real vs Virtual Image confusion
real_virtual_confusion.explanation: Mixing up the characteristics of real (always inverted, formed in front) and virtual (always erect, formed behind) images.
real_virtual_confusion.focus_area: Differentiate between actual ray intersection and projection.

image_position_confusion.title: Image Position Mistake
image_position_confusion.explanation: Incorrectly predicting where the image forms relative to P, F, and C for a given object distance.
image_position_confusion.focus_area: Trace the standard rays to find the intersection point.

image_size_confusion.title: Image Size Mistake
image_size_confusion.explanation: Mixing up the magnification of the image (diminished, magnified, same size) for different object positions.

inverted_erect_confusion.title: Inverted vs Erect Orientation
inverted_erect_confusion.explanation: Incorrectly predicting if the image is upright (erect) or upside-down (inverted).
inverted_erect_confusion.focus_area: Check the sign of the image height.

focus_infinity_confusion.title: At Focus to Infinity Rule
focus_infinity_confusion.explanation: Not knowing that when an object is placed exactly at the focus (F) of a concave mirror, the reflected rays are parallel and the image is formed at infinity.

beyond_c_confusion.title: Beyond C Placement Rule
beyond_c_confusion.explanation: Incorrectly predicting that an object placed beyond C forms an image beyond C. It actually forms a diminished image between C and F.
beyond_c_confusion.focus_area: Observe the intersection point for object beyond C.

parallel_ray_rule_wrong.title: Parallel Ray Rule Mistake
parallel_ray_rule_wrong.explanation: Not knowing that a ray parallel to the principal axis reflects back through the principal focus.
parallel_ray_rule_wrong.focus_area: Draw parallel incident ray reflecting through F.

focus_ray_rule_wrong.title: Focus Ray Rule Mistake
focus_ray_rule_wrong.explanation: Not knowing that a ray passing through the focus reflects parallel to the principal axis.
focus_ray_rule_wrong.focus_area: Draw incident ray through F reflecting parallel.

center_ray_rule_wrong.title: Center Ray Rule Mistake
center_ray_rule_wrong.explanation: Not knowing that a ray passing through the center of curvature retraces its path back after reflection.
center_ray_rule_wrong.focus_area: Draw ray through C retracing itself.

sign_convention_confusion.title: Sign Convention Error
sign_convention_confusion.explanation: Confusing the sign of object distance (always negative), image distance, or focal length under Cartesian sign convention.

image_real_confusion.title: Plane Mirror Image Is Not Real
image_real_confusion.explanation: A plane mirror image is virtual, not real. Light rays only appear to meet behind the mirror when traced backward; no real light reaches there, so the image can never be captured on a screen.
image_real_confusion.focus_area: Show the reflected rays diverging in front of the mirror and their dashed backward extensions meeting behind it.

size_mismatch.title: Plane Mirror Image Size
size_mismatch.explanation: The image formed by a plane mirror is always exactly the same size as the object, no matter how far the object is from the mirror.
size_mismatch.focus_area: Compare the object height and image height directly using matching ray constructions.

distance_confusion.title: Plane Mirror Object-Image Distance
distance_confusion.explanation: The image distance behind a plane mirror is always exactly equal to the object distance in front of it.
distance_confusion.focus_area: Mark equal distances on both sides of the mirror using the perpendicular from object and image to the mirror.

lateral_inversion_confusion.title: Lateral Inversion, Not Upside-Down
lateral_inversion_confusion.explanation: A plane mirror image is laterally inverted -- left and right are swapped -- but it is never upside down. Up stays up, down stays down; only left and right swap.
lateral_inversion_confusion.focus_area: Use an asymmetric left-right shape (like a flag or a letter) to show only the left-right swap, not a vertical flip.

regular_vs_diffused_confusion.title: Regular vs Diffused Reflection
regular_vs_diffused_confusion.explanation: A smooth surface reflects parallel rays so they stay parallel (regular/specular reflection). A rough surface scatters parallel rays in different directions (diffused reflection) -- but every individual ray, on both surfaces, still obeys the law of reflection at its own point of incidence.
regular_vs_diffused_confusion.focus_area: Show several parallel rays reflecting off a smooth surface (staying parallel) versus a jagged surface (scattering), each ray still making equal angles with its own local normal.

rearview_reason_wrong.title: Why Convex Mirrors Are Used for Rear-View
rearview_reason_wrong.explanation: Convex mirrors are used as rear-view and side mirrors because they always form a virtual, erect, diminished image regardless of object distance -- the smaller image fits a wider area of the road into the same mirror, giving a wider field of view than a plane mirror of the same size.
rearview_reason_wrong.focus_area: Compare the field of view captured by a convex mirror versus a plane mirror of the same size.

mirror_formula_sign_error.title: Mirror Formula Sign Substitution Error
mirror_formula_sign_error.explanation: When using 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, every known value must first be given its correct sign (u always negative, f negative for concave and positive for convex) before substituting -- substituting an unsigned magnitude gives a wrong answer even if the formula itself is applied correctly.
mirror_formula_sign_error.focus_area: Write out u, f (and v once found) with their correct signs before and after substituting into the formula.

magnification_sign_error.title: Magnification Sign Interpretation Error
magnification_sign_error.explanation: The sign of magnification m = -v/u tells you the image's nature: positive m means virtual and erect, negative m means real and inverted. Getting the sign of v or u wrong, or misreading the sign of m, leads to describing the wrong kind of image.
magnification_sign_error.focus_area: Compute m from the correctly-signed v and u, then read its sign before describing the image as real/virtual or erect/inverted.
